# Experiment mf01: Marcella damage-stat choice

Base: `2f0f534e8311ee597e516b11c2afca1bbf608060`, bot `leader_party_tuned`.
Candidate directory: `bots/pi_marcella-focus-01/` only. Required report: `IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Hypothesis and evidence

Our Marcella's current shopping classification buys Strength in Monster and Power damage phases. In 30 recent games between the current top-three teams, Marcella appears in 31 team views. Across up to the first ten purchased shard units per appearance, 288/301 are Focus and 13 Health; none Strength. Our 20 latest ranked games have 98 Health and 84 Strength purchases within that same cap, zero Focus. Evidence source: official CLI5 engine3 match summaries cached on PC (not available on Pi). Examples: `01a1a981-8d45-7c14-948a-eda089b61acb` on 00quadrants (Pantheon wins1023–679); `01a1a981-8d45-7696-90d1-c0e070f94ab1` on00swirl (Fish wins1013–60). Leaders use different item families and executors; no causal benefit established.

Hypothesis: changing only Marcella's damage stat to Focus improves ranged/burst opportunities enough to increase score or survival, without the risks of simultaneously copying leaders' item families, roster or coordination. Counterargument: a basic-attack-heavy executor can favour Strength. Under historical kit values a Focus shard adds28 damage per double spell, whereas nine landed basic/reset attacks gain40.5 damage from one Strength shard. The current executor can skip a movement-exclusive spell after movement. We expect the result may be negative; this experiment is intended to discriminate.

## Exact change

In `src/economy.cpp`, add `champion_type::marcella` to the existing local `caster` predicate used by `shop()`. This changes Marcella's second phase from Monster Strength to Monster Focus and later damage phases from Power Strength to Power Focus. Keep first-phase Durability Health, health phases, item family, purchases, thresholds, fuel guards, action ordering and every other champion unchanged. Do not change the caster estimate in `route_plan.cpp`; preserving it isolates actual shopping stat choice, and its mismatch is a known limitation to record.

This should be a tiny coherent patch, not a refactor. No new flags, logging, shared state, coordination, draft, navigation, planner, targeting, or configuration changes. Preserve files outside the candidate directory. Do not touch SDK or dependencies. SDK4 headers at this base have identical callable declarations to isolated SDK5; PC builds/tests with current CLI5 engine3 after compatibility smoke verified exact server build hash.

## Verification and report

Inspect diff against copied baseline. Establish unchanged classification for all other champion types and unchanged shopping phases/families. Run only meaningful available existing checks on Pi; do not fabricate compilation if compiler assets unavailable. The PC performs actual WASM release build, artifact hash, current-engine paired games, and checks purchases in real engine summaries. Do not add a unit test that merely repeats the added predicate. Report exact change, checks actually performed, known execution/routing interactions, and what remains unverified. Leave changes uncommitted; bridge commits/pushes.

## Predeclared PC evaluation

Screen:80 games (8 fixed maps×5 frozen controls×both sides), plus a frozen champion's matched common-opponent control under the same engine. Zero candidate VM faults required. Reject if direct champion result is below8/16 or common-opponent wins are below baseline by more than2/64. Expand only if direct result is at least9/16 AND common wins exceed baseline by at least2/64; otherwise label inconclusive and investigate the mechanism before expansion. These thresholds are screening heuristics, not significance claims.

Record W/L/draw/faults, score differences, Marcella purchases/damage/collected/submitted/lost gems/deaths, map/seed hashes and exact engine/source/WASM identities. No online upload or ranked change based on this screen. Broad and fresh confirmation must follow any screen success.
